title: Pivot tables and crosstabs
summary: Lay a summary out as a grid: rows by one key, columns by another.

steps.title: pivot_table
body: A grouped result with two keys is long and hard to read. A **pivot table** spreads one key across the columns, the layout people expect in a report:
It is `groupby([...]).agg(...)` followed by unstacking, in one call. `fill_value=0` fills combinations that never occurred, and `margins=True` adds an `All` row and column with totals.

code: t = df.pivot_table(index="region", columns="month", values="revenue", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
steps.explain: Columns and rows are sorted labels (`Feb` before `Jan` alphabetically). N in January is 10 + 5.

steps.title: Monthly table
steps.prompt: Write `monthly_table(df)` for columns `region`, `month`, `revenue`. Return a pivot table with one row per region, one column per month **in the order `["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"]`**, summed revenue, and `0` where a region had no sales that month.
solution: t = df.pivot_table(index="region", columns="month", values="revenue", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
hints: Reorder the columns by selecting them: `t[["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"]]`.
template: Dojo.eq("month columns in calendar order", ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"], list(_t.columns))

steps.title: crosstab
body: When you only want to **count** how often two categories occur together, `pd.crosstab` is shorter:
pd.crosstab(df["plan"], df["churned"], normalize="index")    # each row sums to 1
`normalize="index"` turns counts into **rates within each row**: "what fraction of Basic customers churned?" Comparing raw counts is misleading when groups have very different sizes.

steps.explain: Columns are `False, True`. Basic: 2 stayed, 2 churned, a churn rate of 0.5. Pro: nobody churned.

steps.prompt: Average price per category (rows) and size (columns), with totals.
`df.pivot(index="region", columns="month", values="revenue")` raises `ValueError: Index contains duplicate entries`. Why, and what fixes it?
options: Some region and month pair appears in several rows; `pivot` only reshapes, so use `pivot_table` with an `aggfunc` to combine them
steps.explain: `pivot` puts each row into one cell and refuses to guess when two rows land in the same cell. `pivot_table` aggregates them (mean by default, so pass `aggfunc="sum"` for totals).

steps.prompt: Match each tool to its job.
pairs: Grid of summaries, combining duplicate cells
Reshape long to wide when each cell has exactly one row
How often each pair of categories occurs
Turn counts into rates within each row
Add totals as an extra row and column

steps.title: Churn rates
prompt: Write `churn_rates(df)` for columns `plan` and `churned` (`True`/`False`). Return a **dict** `{plan: churn rate}` where the rate is the fraction of that plan's customers who churned, rounded to 2 decimals, using `pd.crosstab(..., normalize="index")`.
A plan where nobody churned has rate `0.0` (careful: then there may be no `True` column at all).
solution: return {plan: round(float(r), 2) for plan, r in rates[True].items()}
hints: `rates = pd.crosstab(df["plan"], df["churned"], normalize="index")`, then the `True` column holds the churn rates.
Check `if True not in rates.columns` for the case where nobody churned.
template: "churned": [True, False, False, True, False, True, False, False]})

steps.title: Report with totals
steps.prompt: Write `sales_grid(df)` for columns `region`, `product`, `revenue`. Return a pivot table of summed revenue with regions as rows, products as columns, missing combinations as `0`, and a `Total` row and column (`margins=True, margins_name="Total"`).
hints: All of it is arguments to one `pivot_table` call.
